orderingSequences.name: equal-stream-sequence-advancing-entity-revision
orderingSequences.why: The in-place PATCH shape in miniature. Equal streamSequence is not staleness when entityRevision moved forward; it is the next revision of the same row.

orderingSequences.name: equal-stream-sequence-equal-entity-revision
orderingSequences.why: A genuinely duplicated frame: same row, same revision. Applying it twice would double-append the delta.

orderingSequences.name: equal-stream-sequence-older-entity-revision
orderingSequences.why: Out-of-order redelivery of an earlier revision of the same row.

orderingSequences.name: equal-stream-sequence-incoming-entity-revision-missing
orderingSequences.why: entityRevision is optional on the wire, so an equal streamSequence with no revision carries no evidence of progress. Fail closed: treating an absent revision as zero would make every such event apply.

orderingSequences.name: equal-stream-sequence-cursor-entity-revision-missing
orderingSequences.why: The mirror case: the cursor was established by an event with no revision, so there is nothing to compare against. Fail closed on this side too.

orderingSequences.name: older-stream-sequence
orderingSequences.why: A lower row offset is unambiguously behind the cursor.

orderingSequences.name: next-stream-sequence
orderingSequences.why: The ordinary advance: the next durable row in the conversation.

orderingSequences.name: stream-sequence-gap
orderingSequences.why: A skipped row can carry an irreversible delete or membership change, so the consumer must resynchronise rather than guess.

orderingSequences.name: production-streaming-burst-offset-14
orderingSequences.why: The captured 2026-07-29 burst. ADR-0023 keeps one channel_messages row per reply and PATCHes it in place, so streamSequence stays "14" for the whole reply and only entityRevision advances. Both SDKs compared streamSequence alone and dropped every event after the first, leaving the bubble empty.

message.body: I checked the pod logs for you. The realtime subscription is up, but every delta after the first one is being dropped before it reaches the reducer

expectProjection.body: I checked the pod logs for you. The realtime subscription is up, but every delta after the first one is being dropped before it reaches the reducer

orderingSequences.name: buffered-replay-of-streaming-burst-offset-14
orderingSequences.why: The captured burst arriving while the conversation hydrates. The page committed the reply row at offset 14 with an empty body, so every buffered delta carries that same offset and not one of them is strictly greater than the commit boundary. What makes them admissible is that the row is already in the projection. Dropping them emptied the bubble on the recovery path exactly as on the live path.

orderingSequences.name: buffered-replay-of-row-the-page-omitted
orderingSequences.why: The offset boundary still owns this case. A page that deliberately did not return a row below its latestOffset — deleted, redacted, filtered — must not have it resurrected out of the buffer. The live gate rejects it too, for the simpler reason that its sequence is behind the cursor.

orderingSequences.name: buffered-replay-of-row-above-the-boundary
orderingSequences.why: A row the page could not have seen. Above the commit boundary the offset comparison is meaningful on its own and the event is new information.
